$y = \lambda x(1-x)$
$x = \lambda y(1-y)$

So $y - x = -\lambda (y - x) (1 - (x + y))$.

Case 1: $y - x = 0$, which means $y = x$. This corresponds to $f(x) = x$.
Case 2: $1 + \lambda (1 - (x + y)) = 0$, which means $1 + \lambda - \lambda(x + y) = 0$, so $x + y = 1 + \frac{1}{\lambda}$.

We are looking for solutions where $f(x) \neq x$, so we must be in Case 2.

Also we have $y = \lambda x(1-x)$.

$x + \lambda x(1-x) = 1 + \frac{1}{\lambda}$.
$\lambda x + \lambda^2 x(1-x) = \lambda + 1$.
$\lambda x + \lambda^2 x - \lambda^2 x^2 = \lambda + 1$.
$-\lambda^2 x^2 + (\lambda^2 + \lambda) x - (\lambda + 1) = 0$.
